findings.fieldOrRegion: field "Text2" (label ", Case No"), widget p1 rect [377.28, 144.21, 506.62, 158.61]
findings.visibleDefect: The boundary fixture prints a case number inside the Text2 widget rect, while the family's own field-classification.json records Text2 as writable:false with factId:null and refusalReason repeating_row_without_indexed_fact, and production-field-map.json lists it under bindingRefusals. populated-fields.json records the write as matter.charges[1].case_number. Read carefully the two are reconcilable -- the refusal is conditional on there being no indexed fact, and the boundary fact set supplies indexed charges -- so this is not called a defect against these bytes. It is recorded because the sibling lane now resolves the same situation the opposite way: D1B's correction narrows the render census to exclude every lane-refused field, which is exactly what removed the KY CHARGE_2 and CHARGE_3 writes in this same review. Two lanes now behave differently on the same question. Pre-existing and unchanged by this cycle: populated-fields.json is byte-identical to the lane head.
findings.likelyOwner: Cross-lane policy — D1C indexed-charge-row mapping vs D1B render-census narrowing
findings.acceptanceCondition: Decide, once, across lanes whether an indexed-charge-row mapping may supersede a name-based binding refusal, and make the classification record state the condition rather than a flat writable:false.
findings.evidenceBasis: text runs decoded from the committed boundary-filled.pdf at the correction branch head and tested against the Text2 widget rect read out of the pack source binary; field-classification.json, production-field-map.json and populated-fields.json read at the same commit and diffed against the lane head

findings.visibleDefect: The ledger gap is substantially closed: the report now carries a boundary refusal for "case number" (refused_exceeds_form_declared_max_length, declaredMaxLength 17, valueLength 60) plus two previously undisclosed DefDate refusals, and refusalsRecorded is 3 where it was absent. But the acceptance condition as written is not met: refusedBelowFloor is still 0, there is no refused_below_readable_floor entry, and the entry names neither the widget rect nor requiredWidthAtMin 210.4 the way the sibling CO/TX entries do. Reading the source binary, the lane's recorded mechanism is the correct primary one — the field declares /MaxLen 17, so the length gate fires before the font-fitting floor is ever reached — but the value also exceeds the widget width at the 6pt floor, and a reader auditing "was anything dropped as unreadably small?" still gets 0.

findings.acceptanceCondition: Either record both constraints for this field (the /MaxLen refusal and the below-floor width refusal, with widget rect and requiredWidthAtMin), or amend the acceptance condition to the /MaxLen mechanism the source binary actually shows and state why refusedBelowFloor is correctly 0.

findings.visibleDefect: The contact sheet is byte-identical to its lane head and was never re-built by the corrected factory. Its raw bytes contain 3 /Type /ObjStm object stream(s), so scanBytesForActiveContent returns inspectable:false and assertInspectableAndClean would raise UninspectableArtifactError rather than emit it. It also carries 33 orphaned /Widget annotation objects copied out of the unsanitized blank panel — /FT, /T, /DA and /Rect intact, /P pointing at a page of the original source form, absent from every page /Annots array but present in the bytes — which is exactly the residue defect B was written to remove. Its contact-sheet-proof.json carries none of the fields the corrected builder emits (no activeContentScan, no panelScans, no panelsSanitizedBeforeEmbedding), confirming it predates the fix. Resolving the object streams myself, I found no XFA, JavaScript, /AA, /OpenAction, /Launch, /SubmitForm, /ImportData or /URI in any object, so this is a fail-closed and residue finding, not an executable-code finding.

families.rationale: The dispositioned defect is cured: the review manifest now records a source pointer that resolves, pack-relative, to a real file whose bytes hash to the recorded sha256, which I confirmed against the extracted pack. Its filled fixtures are clean, byte-inspectable, carry no active-content keys, preserve page count and order, and show every expected participant value. But the family also ships a contact sheet that was never re-built by the corrected factory and does not pass the fail-closed inspection rule this cycle established: object streams in the raw bytes make it uninspectable to the factory's own scanner, and it still carries orphaned widget objects from an unsanitized blank panel. Reviewing on the bytes rather than on the classification, it cannot be approved.

findings.visibleDefect: The contact sheet is byte-identical to its lane head and was never re-built by the corrected factory. Its raw bytes contain 2 /Type /ObjStm object stream(s), so scanBytesForActiveContent returns inspectable:false and assertInspectableAndClean would raise UninspectableArtifactError rather than emit it. It also carries 33 orphaned /Widget annotation objects copied out of the unsanitized blank panel — /FT, /T, /DA and /Rect intact, /P pointing at a page of the original source form, absent from every page /Annots array but present in the bytes — which is exactly the residue defect B was written to remove. Its contact-sheet-proof.json carries none of the fields the corrected builder emits (no activeContentScan, no panelScans, no panelsSanitizedBeforeEmbedding), confirming it predates the fix. Resolving the object streams myself, I found no XFA, JavaScript, /AA, /OpenAction, /Launch, /SubmitForm, /ImportData or /URI in any object, so this is a fail-closed and residue finding, not an executable-code finding.

findings.visibleDefect: The family is unchanged from its lane head: git diff over its artifact directory is empty, and it emits no filled fixture or contact sheet. rcap-pdf-anchor-capture.mjs is byte-identical to the D0 base (blob 25358c46fb0e894b43ccd15a1689f257f9131e88) on all seven correction branches, and loadFonts() still contains no /ToUnicode or /Encoding /Differences handling. Reading the source binary directly, the text layer decodes cleanly for me, including the subset fonts on the CrRLJ forms, so the "no extractable text" premise remains false.
